items.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: we went up there to visit Grandma Twy, and when she saw us she said that they were having the first ever Elders’ Peace Conference. The indigenous elders were coming from all around. The requirements were that they had to come, and tell a story and not bring any anger, and they had to tell a joke. We were there, and she was amazing, Grandma Twy. Grandma Twy was a jazz drummer apparently. She was a little thing, about four feet something. She played drums so good when she was kid that she played with…[Woody…
Yeah, Corey. The bassist was… We’ll get that.
